inspiration: Fixed world tick: the world ticks every 600 ms (src/engine/World.ts line 120), and each cycle runs in a stated order: client input (line 355), NPC event queue for spawn and despawn triggers (line 358), NPC processing (line 367), zones with loc and obj respawn (line 390), then cleanup (line 415). This maps onto the Frankendom sub-line 'server tick: fixed step, input intake, per-tick NPC budget': the fixed step and input intake exist, but I found no per-tick NPC budget. processNpcs turns every NPC in the list each tick (World.ts line 667). That is a gap to design, not a copy. Mechanism, not art.

Respawn speeds up with population: removeNpc and removeObj scale the respawn duration by (4000 minus players) over 4000, with players clamped at 2000 (World.ts lines 1733 and 1734, applied at lines 1313 and 1523). A busy zone refills faster, at most twice as fast at the cap. The code comment says the author is not sure the cap is right (World.ts line 1732). Zone population (parity row 23): a busy-zone respawn lever with no extra art.

Three lifecycle states (src/engine/entity/EntityLifeCycle.ts lines 2 to 4): FOREVER (never respawns), RESPAWN (engine-placed, comes back after a delay), DESPAWN (script-placed, removed for good). Spawn caps and despawn policy can key off the state. No despawn grace timer exists in this code (a search for grace found none), so the grace-on-empty rule in row 23 is ours to design.

Respawn countdown is gated: Npc.turn decrements its lifecycle tick only while the NPC is not delayed (src/engine/entity/Npc.ts line 121). A delayed NPC's respawn clock stops. Check whether that is intended before copying; it may be a defect.
Lifecycle tick clamps to at least one tick (src/engine/entity/Entity.ts line 40): a zero or tiny duration cannot become zero. A small guard worth copying.

Recolour variants of effects as text config: the spot-animation pack reads model, anim, resizeh and resizev, and recol pairs (tools/pack/config/SpotAnimConfig.ts lines 77 and 123). Effects as data, packed for both client and server.

briefs.label: Population-scaled respawn clock (zone pulse)
briefs.why: Quiet zones refill slowly and busy zones refill fast, with no extra art and one formula.
briefs.keep: a linear scale in player count; a hard clamp so the scale stops growing; the same rule for NPCs and objects
briefs.change: our clamp point and floor (for example a floor at a quarter of the base time); a per-zone coverage value; a despawn grace timer on empty zones

briefs.label: Three-state entity lifecycle
briefs.why: Splitting permanent, respawning and script-placed entities keeps the spawn rules readable.
briefs.keep: permanent, respawn and script-placed as three distinct states
briefs.change: our names; a fourth state for a timed event or boss lock; the state drives the cap rules

briefs.label: Recolour-variant effect record
briefs.why: One model, one animation and a few colour pairs give many effect variants with no new art.
briefs.keep: model, animation, resize and colour pairs as text fields
briefs.change: our own colour pair set and our resize values; our effect names; a per-rarity palette

briefs.label: Fixed-step turn order
briefs.why: A stated turn order (input, triggers, NPCs, zones, cleanup) makes timing bugs easy to find.
briefs.keep: a fixed step length; a named order of phases; cleanup as the last phase
briefs.change: our own phase list, with the boss phase separate; a per-tick NPC budget that defers work instead of dropping it
